method: Each surface was driven with the gateway or a stub listening behind a temporary public tunnel. A request counts as 'reached' only if the capture proxy logged it. UI messages are quoted as shown. Hosts are replaced with placeholders; the tunnel was deleted afterwards.

aliases: foundry-luna -> Foundry GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API
foundry-haiku -> Foundry Claude Haiku 5.5 through the Anthropic route

ide_reading: With the Azure slot on, GPT-5.2 was no longer blocked by the plan gate and was sent to the own-key path, which then failed on the dummy key. Non-Azure hosts never received a request. A run with a real key was not made because it needs the owner's approval to store a Foundry key in Cursor.
capture_log_review: The capture logs for the whole round hold 8 requests, all sent by the tester: four local checks with PowerShell and four requests through the tunnel. Two of the tunnel requests set User-Agent: Cursor/1.0 by hand to mimic the documented Cursor caller (curl-style headers, no Accept-Encoding, sent before any key was saved in Cursor). None came from Cursor's servers.
